title: Identification of Heterogeneous Peer Effects
abstract: arXiv:2410.14317v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We develop a peer effects model in which each peer's influence depends on their outcome rank within the peer group. Unlike existing models, it allows non-monotonic effects across ranks. The model admits a unique equilibrium, and its parameters can be identified using peers' exogenous characteristics. We introduce a parsimonious quantile-dependent specification and develop a specification test to guide model selection. Applying the model to student outcomes in Add Health reveals heterogeneous, often non-monotonic spillovers. Counterfactual analysis shows that allowing for non-monotonic peer effects changes the rankings of influential students relative to existing models. Our R package, QuantilePeer, implements these methods.

translated_title: 异质性同伴效应的识别
translated_abstract: 我们开发了一个同伴效应模型，其中每个同伴的影响力取决于其在同伴群体中的结果排名。与现有模型不同，该模型允许跨排名的非单调效应。该模型存在唯一均衡，且其参数可以通过同伴的外生特征进行识别。我们引入了一个简约的分位数依赖设定，并开发了一个设定检验以指导模型选择。将该模型应用于Add Health数据中的学生表现，揭示了异质的、通常为非单调的溢出效应。反事实分析表明，与现有模型相比，允许非单调同伴效应会改变有影响力学生的排名。我们的R包QuantilePeer实现了这些方法。
tldr: 本文提出了一个同伴影响力取决于其在群体中结果排名的同伴效应模型，允许非单调效应并能用外生特征识别参数，应用于Add Health数据揭示了异质且非单调的溢出效应，并证明这会改变反事实分析中有影响力学生的排名。
en_tdlr: We develop a peer effects model where each peer's influence depends on their outcome rank within the peer group, allowing non-monotonic effects; applied to Add Health, it reveals heterogeneous spillovers and changes the rankings of influential students in counterfactual analysis.
